steps.note: Make the app store '' instead of NULL for guest orders; the rolling update finishes before the next step.
Let terminating old pods finish in-flight requests (3 s drain + up to 2 s statement timeout).

Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: enforced for new writes from now on, no table scan. Needs a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, so take it with a short lock_timeout and retry instead of queueing behind traffic.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND conname = 'orders_email_not_null') THEN RETURN; END IF; FOR i IN 1..200 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '100ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add the check constraint'; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill NULL emails to '' in id ranges of 50,000, committing after each batch: short transactions, no long row locks, no table lock.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint := 0; hi bigint; BEGIN SELECT max(id) INTO hi FROM orders; WHILE lo <= hi LOOP UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE id > lo AND id <= lo + 50000 AND email IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + 50000; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the check constraint: full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL: Postgres 17 uses the validated check to skip the scan, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is held only for a moment. Then drop the now-redundant check. Both with short lock_timeout and retry.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..200 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '100ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to set NOT NULL'; END $$; DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..200 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '100ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS orders_email_not_null; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to drop the check constraint'; END $$;
